blocks.text: **Biotechnology** uses living organisms/systems to make products and processes, while **nanotechnology** manipulates matter at the **atomic/molecular (nano) scale**. Both are transformative across health, agriculture, industry and the environment.

rows: Vaccines, insulin, gene therapy, diagnostics, monoclonal antibodies.
1–100 nm scale; drug delivery, nano-materials, electronics, water purification.
**DBT (Dept of Biotechnology); BIRAC; nano — Nano Mission**.

prelimsPointers: **Biotechnology** — use of living systems to make products (colour codes: red-medical, green-agriculture, white-industrial, blue-marine).
**Bt cotton** — India's only approved commercial GM crop (uses Bacillus thuringiensis gene).
**Nanotechnology** works at the **1–100 nanometre** scale.
Applications — **vaccines, insulin, gene therapy, GM crops, drug delivery, water purification**.
**Department of Biotechnology (DBT)** & **BIRAC** promote biotech; **Nano Mission** for nanotech.
**PCR, recombinant DNA, CRISPR** are key biotech tools.
**Tissue culture** enables mass plant propagation.

glossary.definition: The use of living organisms or systems to develop products and processes.
The manipulation of matter at the 1-100 nanometre scale.
A genetically modified cotton carrying a bacterial gene for pest resistance.

sections.heading: Ethical, social & legal issues & government policies

blocks.text: Biotechnology raises **ethical, social and legal (ELSI)** concerns — over GM foods, biosafety, gene editing, data privacy and equity — regulated in India by a framework of **biosafety rules and regulatory bodies**.

rows: GM-food safety, gene editing of humans, cloning, designer babies, consent.
Biopiracy, farmers' rights, IPR/patents on life, biosafety.
**Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee** — approves GMO release (under MoEFCC).
**Biosafety rules (1989); proposed biotech regulator; Cartagena Protocol** (biosafety).

prelimsPointers: **GEAC (Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee)** — apex GMO regulator (under MoEFCC).
**Bt brinjal** — approval put under moratorium (2010) over safety concerns.
**Cartagena Protocol** — biosafety (safe transfer/handling of GMOs).
**PPV&FR Act, 2001** — protects plant varieties & **farmers' rights**.
Ethical issues — **GM safety, human gene editing, cloning, biopiracy**.
**Nagoya Protocol** — access & benefit-sharing of genetic resources.
**Biological Diversity Act 2002** guards against biopiracy.

glossary.definition: The Genetic Engineering Appraisal Committee, India's apex regulator for GMO release.
The unauthorised commercial exploitation of biological resources or traditional knowledge.
The international agreement on the safe handling and transfer of GMOs.

sections.heading: Genetic engineering — issues & impact on human life, health & environment

blocks.text: **Genetic engineering** directly modifies an organism's **DNA** to achieve desired traits. It powers advances in **medicine, agriculture and industry** — but its impact on **human health, the environment and ethics** is closely debated.

rows: **Recombinant DNA, PCR, gene cloning, CRISPR-Cas9 (gene editing)**.
**Gene therapy, insulin/vaccines, genetic diagnosis, personalised medicine**.
**GM crops** (pest/drought resistance, higher yield, biofortification — Golden Rice).
Gene flow to wild species, loss of biodiversity, superweeds/pests.

prelimsPointers: **Recombinant DNA technology** = combining DNA from different sources (genetic engineering).
**CRISPR-Cas9** — precise gene-editing tool (Nobel Chemistry 2020).
**Gene therapy** treats disease by correcting faulty genes.
**Golden Rice** — genetically biofortified with **Vitamin A**.
Health concerns — **allergenicity, antibiotic-resistance markers**; environmental — **gene flow, biodiversity loss**.
**GM crops** in India — only **Bt cotton** is commercially approved.
**Human germline editing** is ethically restricted worldwide.

glossary.definition: The direct modification of an organism's DNA to introduce desired traits.
Treating disease by correcting or replacing defective genes.
